claims.title: Higher-order matching and a cubic moment obstruction
claims.claim: A matching-support amplitude budget and section-oscillation bound are proved in the note. The rare-gate construction Z=(U−p)Σ_j B_j refutes a distribution-independent fourth-moment bound for overlapping degree-two increments.
assumptions: finite product and bounded degree for structural lemmas
U∼Bernoulli(p), independent fair signs B_j for counterexample
claims.mechanism: Independent disjoint supports preserve parity-coupled cancellations; a shared rare coordinate invalidates a naive overlapping-increment moment estimate.
claims.evidence: Elementary mathematical arguments and explicit counterexample in the checked-in note; no independent human referee or claimed Lean theorem.
claims.source_detail: Explicit exact moment formulas and two elementary structural lemmas.
claims.audit: Independently check parity-coupling assumptions, section-oscillation constants and exact fourth moments; test codegree-sensitive replacements against rare-gate stars.
limitations: Refutes a proposed proof operator, not the degree-three influence conjecture
Global originality and referee review open

claims.title: Log-free Kaczmarz best-iterate projection bound
claims.claim: For every consistent real Ax*=b and K>=1, max-normalized-residual greedy Kaczmarz satisfies min_{0<=t<K} ||Ay_t-b|| <= ||A||_F ||y_0-x*||/sqrt(K); consequently K<=ceil(n/epsilon^2) for delta=epsilon||A||op. This is a successful-prefix-iterate existence result.
assumptions: consistent real linear system with A nonzero, zero rows skipped
each iteration chooses a row with maximal squared normalized residual
orthogonal projections; one selected iterate among the first K, not necessarily the final iterate
claims.mechanism: Projection Pythagoras gives a per-step decrease; max normalized residual dominates its row-norm weighted average; telescoping bounds the sum of squared residuals, so one prefix iterate meets the threshold.
claims.evidence: Written complete elementary argument; 240 exact-rational consistent systems with 12 greedy steps each (2,880 total steps), 1D sharpness control; finite checker CI and site checks track reproducibility, not global proof certification.
claims.source_detail: Proof, scope and provenance in same folder PROOF.md; exact checker exact_audit.py. Chat proof packet SHA-256 0245feee6e886cbfff2eb717d33ecbf8dd1d8bc8efc055713bd4ba64325a5587.
claims.audit: Independent mathematical proof review and exhaustive dated priority search in earlier greedy-Kaczmarz work; ask problem author to confirm interpretation and novelty before any publication.
limitations: Classical maximum-distance Kaczmarz selection and energy identity are credited; global novelty is unverified
No fixed-final-iterate high-probability guarantee or end-to-end row-selection runtime claim
No independent human referee or Lean formalization, and no historical Original Finding promotion

claims.title: Exact consecutive 4-shuffle forcing threshold (N4 = 20)
claims.claim: Every permutation of length 20 has a consecutive factor of length 8 or 12 partitionable into four equal-size subsequences with a common relative-order pattern. A concrete length-19 permutation avoids every eligible factor (length 8, 12, 16), so N4=20.
assumptions: distinct permutation entries and standardization of consecutive factors
four disjoint increasing-index subsequences of identical pattern and size at least two
ordinary k=4 shuffle definition, not the conjecture for all k
claims.mechanism: Perfect-matching classification of 8-patterns; 5040-state avoidance factor graph with 2632 edges; all 302 twenty-position bad-eight paths force a 12-entry common-triple exact cover using only local comparisons; independently checked 19-term witness.
claims.evidence: Clean source ZIP re-extracted; eight hashes verified; original independent finite checker re-run successfully. Public standalone Python checker reconstructs all 302 upper paths and 24 lower factors without JSON. No external non-author referee or Lean formalization.
claims.source_detail: Companion complete mathematical proof in README.md and standalone verifier verify_four_shuffle.py. Original full PDF/ZIP and 302-row data JSON supplied in chat but not yet publicly deposited as GitHub binary assets.
claims.audit: Independently reconstruct all 2632 edges, enumerate all 302 bad-eight paths, verify forced 12-pattern partitions under partial comparison information and every lower-witness factor. Compare all post-2024 literature before claiming originality.
limitations: Only k=4 is covered; the general k-shuffle conjecture remains open
Inherited factor-graph and matching method credited to Bevan, Elvey Price and Felsner
Exact finite checker and internally independent replay are not external human mathematical review or global priority clearance
